newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia reserves $20 bln, of which $2.5 bln gold.
newsitem.headline: Russia reserves $20 bln, of which $2.5 bln gold.

text.p: Russia's gross gold and currency reserves currently total $20 billion, of which $2.5 billion are in gold, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Monday.

"At the moment gold and foreign currency reserves are $20 billion, of which $2.5 billion are gold, and the rest in currency," Dubinin said in an address to the lower house of parliament, the State Duma.
"During the last six months the situation has stabilised. We will buy more currency than we sell in order to boost our gold/currency reserves," Dubinin said.

He said gold and currency reserves last year fell to $11.2 billion from $12.6 billion at the start of 1996. Dubinin said on June 5 that Russia's gross gold and foreign currency reserves totalled around $19 billion.

He said in his address on Monday that inflation would slow during the summer months, and that M2 money supply, including bank deposits and cash in circulation, would increase by a third this year, or 100-108 trillion roubles, after rising by 75 trillion last year.
